summary: This change fixes a subtle bug so that user lookups are always performed consistently, improving reliability for all callers.

items.title: The None check still runs before the lookup
items.before: get_active_user checked user_id is None and returned before calling lookup.
items.after: get_active_user still checks user_id is None before calling lookup, guaranteeing lookup is never invoked for a missing id.
items.statement: The None-check guard clause still runs before lookup(user_id) is called, so lookup is never invoked for a missing user id.

items.title: Calling lookup with None is safe
items.after: lookup(None) safely returns an empty record with no side effects, so this reorder introduces no new failure mode.
items.statement: Calling lookup with a None id is safe and simply returns an empty record, so no new failure mode is introduced by this change.

items.title: General module context
items.statement: This function lives within the broader user management module, which is responsible for many aspects of the user lifecycle across the codebase in a modular, maintainable, and well-organized fashion that supports the team's long-term engineering goals.
